main_text.l: à quibus scatet fæcibus repurgarent, ut conta-
minatiorem multo nobis exhiberent, sanioribus ex-
punctis sequiora inseruerunt[?]; quæque verso stylo
D. Bucerus eximiæ pietatis & reconditæ eruditionis
Theologus olim delevit, ea repofuerunt; adeo ut
nullus sit in farraginea[?] pontificiorum errorum mole
cuius in ea fere maturam messem aut fermentem sal-
tem oculatus & judiciosus lector non deprehendet.
Hinc novorum motuum & tot malorum origo quæ
exterorum aures[?] atque animos implevit. Nam cum
Regio diplomate in eas angustias Pastores & popu-
lus conjecti essent, ut vel perduellionis crimen subire
vel illam liturgiam contra jusjurandum, fidem, Ecc-
lesiæ & Patriæ instituta amplecti cogerentur, effectum
est, ut Regni omnes Ordines quorum jamdu-
dum in tolerandis Episcopis patientia obrutuit, hu-
jus liturgiæ experrecti nuncio de profligandis
corruptelis & primæva puritate restituenda consilium
inierint. Regem itaque Serenissimum complurimis
supplicibus libellis & sanctiorem ejus Senatum ro-
gare, orare, hortari non destiterunt, ut afflictæ Ec-
clesiæ succurrerent, in Episcopos vero tantorum ma-
lorum authores serio animadverterent. Dum tardius
auxilium parari, supplicibus libellis non responderi,
postulata sua nihil pensi haberi cernerent; in se al-
tius descendunt, mentis latebras penitus excutiunt,
violati fœderis memoria conscientias pungit, lanc-
inat, perfodit; quare seria pœnitentia ducti fœdus
cum fidei confessione renovare statuerunt; quæ Chiro-
graphis primo consignarunt, deinde solenni indicto
jejunio jurejurando sublatis dexteris multo cum ge-
mitu & lachrymis publice in templis confirmarunt.
Dum hæc aguntur missus est à Serenissimo Rege
Marchio Hamiltonius ad controversias has cognoscen-
das, lites componendas & tempestates omnes in
tranquillum redigendas: cujus ope & industria hoc
confe-

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. Uncertain readings: "sequiora inseruerunt" (ink blur over the word that could be read differently), "farraginea" (the final letters are obscured by a stain), "aures" (the word after "exterorum" is partly cut by a fold, so the reading is a guess). The word "salutem" is broken at the line end as "sal-/tem" and is read as "saltem", since it fits the sense. The page has no printed page number. No marginal notes are printed.
